personality: 8 Hand-Drawn organic warmth fused with 4 Tactile / Playful structure for high accessibility
personality_one_liner: A warm, natural, and highly accessible cognitive wellness space that feels like a supportive companion, not a clinical tool.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing is critical for elderly users to prevent accidental taps. Elements should never feel cramped.

navigation: stack_only (Hub-and-spoke for Patient mode), bottom_tabs (for Caregiver & ASHA modes)

dont's: Avoid glassmorphism completely. Seniors require solid, high-contrast surfaces without distracting visual layers or blurs.

screens.name: Role Selection (Entry)
screens.purpose: Simple, large-touch-target screen to select Patient, Family Caregiver, or ASHA Health Worker.

states.loading: Centered loading spinner with botanical leaf icon.
states.error: Cannot load roles, large 'Try Again' button.

screens.layout: Vertical list of massive, padded cards (using surfaceSecondary) for each role. Each card has a distinct pastel tint (brandSecondary/brandTertiary) and large Phosphor icon. Stick a prominent Caregiver login option at the bottom.

screens.name: Patient Home Dashboard
screens.purpose: Primary navigation hub for the patient, extremely simple and warm.

states.error: Failed to load dashboard, gentle retry button.

screens.layout: 2x2 grid (or 1-column stack if needed for tap size) of oversized tiles taking up most of the screen: Memories, Games, Relaxation, Daily Life. Each tile uses a soft pastel background with a large, friendly image or icon, and very large text. Settings icon isolated at top right.

screens.name: Caregiver Dashboard
screens.purpose: Functional dashboard for family caregivers or ASHA workers to monitor and manage patient engagement.

states.loading: Skeleton list of recent alerts and reports.
states.error: Could not sync data, retry button.

screens.layout: Standard mobile layout. Quick stat summary at top (Reports, Patient Profile). Scrollable list of recent Alerts and Calendar events below. Bottom tab navigation for switching contexts.

hero_patient.alt: Happy senior couple playing in a field

tile_relaxation.alt: Person looking at a calm sunset in nature

instructions_to_main_agent: ACCESSIBILITY OVERRIDE: The typography scale is significantly larger than standard defaults. Base text is 18pt, and all UI elements must accommodate this without clipping.
TOUCH TARGETS: All clickable elements (buttons, cards, icons) must have a minimum hit area of 60x60pt to support older adults. Use padding and hitSlop aggressively.

PATIENT NAVIGATION: Avoid bottom tabs for Patient Mode. Use a 'hub-and-spoke' architecture where the Patient Home contains large tiles, and all sub-screens have a prominent, oversized 'Back' or 'Home' button at the top.
CAREGIVER NAVIGATION: Caregiver and ASHA modes should use standard bottom tab navigation, as they are used by more digitally literate users.

COLOR USAGE: Use the muted botanical green (brand) and cream (surface) heavily to create a calming, non-clinical environment. Rely on the darker sage (brandPrimary) for primary text/buttons to ensure WCAG AAA contrast.
NO GLASSMORPHISM: Seniors need solid, distinct separation of elements. Do not use blurs or translucent sheets.
GENTLE ANIMATIONS: Use React Native Reanimated for soft, slow transitions (e.g., 300-400ms fades or springs), avoiding fast snapping which can be disorienting.
FONT WEIGHTS: Avoid thin fonts entirely; stick to 400 and 500 weights for `Nunito`, ensuring readability.
